findings.source_quote: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐδιψύχησαν καὶ ἐδιχοστάτησαν.
findings.english_quote: Some among them wavered and caused divisions.
findings.issue: “Caused divisions” introduces causative agency: it says these people produced divisions. The selected Greek describes their being divided or at variance, without separately asserting that they caused divisions among others.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Some among them wavered and were at odds.” Review this proposed wording afresh against both verbs before adopting it.

findings.source_quote: οὗτοι ἔτι ἔχουσι μετάνοιαν ἐὰν ταχὺ μετανοήσωσι, καὶ ἔσται αὐτῶν ἡ κατοικία εἰς τὸν πύργον
findings.english_quote: These still have an opportunity to repent if they repent quickly. Their dwelling will be in the tower.
findings.issue: The sentence break leaves the tower dwelling as a standalone, unqualified prediction. In the source, that dwelling belongs to the quick-repentance outcome. Although the following sentences describe other outcomes, readers should not have to reconstruct the condition governing this assertion.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “If they repent quickly, they still have an opportunity to repent, and their dwelling will be in the tower.” Alternatively, retain the existing first sentence and explicitly condition the second: “If they do, their dwelling will be in the tower.” Review the replacement afresh for the source’s relationship between opportunity and repentance.

findings.source_quote: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐδιψύχησαν καὶ ἐδιχοστάτησαν.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this wording assigns causative responsibility for divisions where the selected Greek describes being divided or at variance.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Some of them wavered and were at odds.” Review the proposed rendering afresh before adopting it.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard introduces causative agency in the description of division; the simplified does so independently and also loosens the condition governing dwelling in the tower. Otherwise, the rod groups, proportions, negations, death warnings, speaker continuity, and contextual repentance terminology are preserved. The notes distinguish the working proportion correction from the reported Athos alternative and disclose the added “still” in paragraph 5. Their witness references are treated as attributed reports, not as authenticated manuscript readings or an exhaustive collation. Proposed replacements remain subject to fresh review.
